message.content:
In the Nxeon codebase at /opt/nxeon (Next.js/TypeScript/Prisma app), VPS servers have a "Show password" feature on their dashboard detail page that reveals the server's root password to the customer. Game servers (a separate product line) do NOT have this feature at all, even though the shared deployment email template (lib/email-templates.ts's `serverDeployed`) tells every customer "read it from the dashboard under 'Show password'".

I need you to find and report back, in detail:

1. Where exactly the VPS "Show password" feature lives — the server action(s) that fetch/decrypt the password (likely something using `lib/sftp.ts`'s `serverRootPassword()` or `lib/crypto-box.ts`'s decrypt, given those are used elsewhere in this codebase), and the exact file(s) + line numbers.
2. The client-side component(s) that render the "Show password" button/reveal UI for VPS servers — exact file path(s), and enough of the actual code (copy the real JSX/logic) that I can replicate the same interaction pattern (e.g. is it a button that reveals inline, a modal, does it require a confirm/re-auth step, is there rate-limiting or audit logging on the reveal action?).
3. Where VPS servers' detail page lives (app/dashboard/servers/[id]/... or similar) and exactly where in that page the "Show password" UI is inserted, so I can find the equivalent spot on the game-server detail page.
4. Confirm: does the game-server dashboard have a per-server detail page at all today? Earlier investigation found only app/dashboard/games/page.tsx (a list page) — check app/dashboard/games/ thoroughly (including any [id] dynamic route) and components/customer/Game*.tsx to confirm whether a per-server detail page exists or needs to be created from scratch.
5. Check how the game server's root password is actually stored/retrievable at all — grep for where a game server's Server row gets its password set at provision time (worker/index.ts or similar) to confirm it uses the same storage mechanism (encrypted secret) as VPS servers, so the same decrypt/reveal action can be reused as-is.

Report back with exact file paths, line numbers, and relevant code snippets so I can implement the same "Show password" feature on the game-server dashboard without re-deriving any of this from scratch. Do not make any edits — this is research only.

I have everything needed. Here is the full research report. ## Summary The good news: almost nothing needs to be built from scratch. Game servers and VPS servers are **the same `Server` DB row and the same detail-page route** (`app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx`). The page already branches on `isGameServer` and already computes/decrypts `rootPassword` before that branch — it just never passes it into the game-server render path. Storage/decrypt mechanics are 100% shared already. --- ### 1. Where "Show password" decrypt lives (server side) - `/opt/nxeon/lib/sftp.ts:28-32` ```ts export function serverRootPassword( server: { rootPassword: string | null; rootPasswordEnc?: string | null } ): string | null { return decryptSecret(server.rootPasswordEnc) ?? server.rootPassword; } ``` - Decrypt primitive: `/opt/nxeon/lib/crypto-box.ts:35-47` — `decryptSecret()` (AES-256-GCM, key derived from `AUTH_SECRET`). Returns `null` on any failure so callers fall back safely. - **There is no separate "reveal" server action.** The decrypt happens once, server-side, at page render: `app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx:106`: ```ts const rootPassword = serverRootPassword(server); ``` This plaintext is passed as a prop into a client component; the "reveal" is purely a client-side `useState` toggle on already-fetched plaintext. **No rate-limiting, no re-auth/confirm, no audit log fires on the reveal click itself** — the only gate is the page's own ownership check at `page.tsx:102`: ```ts if (!server || (server.userId !== user.id && user.role !== "ADMIN")) notFound(); ``` - The one password-related action that *does* exist is **reset**, not reveal: `lib/actions-server.ts:231-245` `resetRootPassword(serverId)` — queues a `PASSWORD_RESET` job and writes an `auditLog` (`action: "server.password_reset"`). This is unrelated to the reveal itself but sits right next to it in the UI. ### 2. Client component that renders "Show password" File: `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/ServerAccess.tsx` (full file, 78 lines). The relevant piece, `RevealPassword` (lines 62-77): ```tsx export function RevealPassword({ password }: { password: string }) { const [shown, setShown] = useState(false); return ( {shown && } ); } ``` It's a **plain inline toggle button** (no modal, no confirm, no re-fetch) — click reveals the plaintext (already sitting in the client bundle's props) in place of dots, and reveals a `CopyText` copy button next to it. `CopyText` (lines 6-22) and `ResetPasswordButton` (lines 24-60, calls `resetRootPassword` from `@/lib/actions-server` behind a `window.confirm`) live in the same file. ### 3. VPS detail page — exact insertion point File: `app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx`. The "Access" card in the `overview` tab, lines 266-304: ```tsx

Access

... SSH command ...
Root password
{rootPassword ? ( ) : ( — )}
... IP ...

Lost access or rotating credentials? Generate a fresh root password.

``` This whole `overview` block (built starting at line 259) is only reachable via `` at line 1140-1154, which is inside the **non-game-server return path** (line 1079 onward). The imports needed are already at the top: `RevealPassword`, `CopyText`, `ResetPasswordButton` from `@/components/customer/ServerAccess` (line 20). ### 4. Confirmed: no per-game-server detail page exists separately — it's the same route, just a different render branch - `app/dashboard/games/` contains **only** `page.tsx` (a list page) — no `[id]` route. Confirmed via `find app/dashboard/games -type f`. - That list page's "Manage" links point straight at the shared route: `app/dashboard/games/page.tsx:108` → `href={`/dashboard/servers/${s.id}`}`. - Inside `app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx`, `isGameServer` is computed at line 209 (`GAME_FAMILIES.includes(server.osTemplate.family as GameFamily)`, imported from `@/lib/games` at line 52), and `rootPassword` is already computed above that at line 106 — so it's in scope. When `isGameServer` is true, the function takes a completely separate return path at **lines 1039-1076**, rendering `` from `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/gamepanel/GameServerPanel.tsx` instead of ``. `GameServerPanel`'s tabs are `overview | console | files | mods | plugins | backups | players | settings | activity` (lines 24-34 of that file) — **none of them show the root password anywhere**: - `GameOverview.tsx` (`components/customer/gamepanel/GameOverview.tsx`) shows a `Connect` field (`data.connect`, ip:port) but no password/SSH. - `GamePanelHeader.tsx` shows a "Connect" copy button (`data.connect`) but no password. - The inline `gameSettingsPanel` built at `page.tsx:987-1037` has cards for Server name, Game Settings, Auto-update, Schedules, Startup/env (marked "coming soon"), and Network (shows `connect` string only) — again, no password/SSH/root-access card at all. - `GameHeaderData` type (`components/customer/gamepanel/types.ts:14-42`) has no password field. So: **the per-game-server detail page already exists** (it's this same file/route), it just needs the Access/password UI added somewhere in the game branch — most naturally as a small "Access" card inside `gameSettingsPanel` (or a new field threaded into `GameOverview`/`GamePanelHeader`), reusing `RevealPassword`/`CopyText`/`ResetPasswordButton` exactly as imported at line 20, and passing the already-computed `rootPassword` (line 106) and `sshCommand`/`sftpHost`/`sftpPort` (already computed above line 209 for the VPS path) into that new card. ### 5. Confirmed: game servers use the identical encrypted-password storage mechanism There is **one** provisioning function, `provision(job)` in `/opt/nxeon/worker/index.ts` (starts line 418), used for both VPS and game servers — no per-product branching on password handling: - Sandbox path, `worker/index.ts:436-440`: `const password = generatePassword(); ... data: { ..., rootPassword: null, rootPasswordEnc: encryptSecret(password), ... }` - Real-VM path, `worker/index.ts:482` and `504-507`: same `rootPasswordEnc: encryptSecret(password)` write to `Server.rootPasswordEnc`. - Password reset (`worker/index.ts:1209` and `1238`) and restore flows write to the same `rootPasswordEnc` column via `encryptSecret`. - `worker/game-control.ts:41-42`, `worker/game-mods.ts:168-169`, `worker/game-config.ts:176-177`, `worker/game-update.ts` etc. all select `rootPassword`/`rootPasswordEnc` off the same `Server` row and decrypt via `serverRootPassword()`/`decryptSecret()` to SSH into the box for game-specific operations (mod installs, config edits, updates) — proving the game-server worker code already depends on this exact same encrypted secret today. Conclusion: `serverRootPassword(server)` / `decryptSecret()` can be reused **as-is, unmodified**, for game servers — the value is already correctly populated in `Server.rootPasswordEnc` for every game server the same way it is for VPS. ### Practical plan for replicating the feature on the game dashboard 1. In `app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx`, inside the `if (isGameServer) { ... }` block (starts line 946), add an "Access" card (reusing `RevealPassword`, `CopyText`, `ResetPasswordButton`, `SftpAccess` — already imported at lines 20/26-ish) using the `rootPassword`, `sshCommand`/`overlayConnect`, `sftpHost`, `sftpPort`, `dedicated` values that are already computed earlier in the function (lines 106, 197-221) and currently only used by the VPS branch/overlay. 2. Simplest slot: append it into `gameSettingsPanel` (lines 987-1037) next to the existing "Network" card, or pass a new `accessPanel` prop into `GameServerPanel` and add an "Access" entry to its `TABS` array (`GameServerPanel.tsx:24-34`) alongside `settingsPanel`. 3. No backend/worker/schema changes are required — the encrypted password is already stored and already decryptable via the existing `serverRootPassword()` helper for every game server.
